Many belts made after nineteen seventy-four use an inertia reel that permits comfortable movement but locks when the vehicle slows abruptly. narration.text: Child safety seats spread collision forces over a broader area of the child's body. A properly restrained child is less likely to distract the driver. Alaska generally requires occupants of motor vehicles to use safety belts, subject to the listed legal exceptions. An unbelted passenger who is at least eighteen may receive a citation, while the driver is responsible for occupants younger than sixteen. The driver must supply and properly secure the required restraint before transporting a child younger than sixteen. A child younger than one, or an older child weighing less than twenty pounds, must use an approved rear-facing child safety seat according to manufacturer instructions. A child aged at least one but younger than five, weighing at least twenty pounds, must use an approved child restraint according to manufacturer instructions.
